title: The Plan to Discredit the Florida Recount

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重新构想者》，这是一个专注于热爱设计及与其相关的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代夜总会当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带300件你最珍爱的传家宝去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个像美丽的50岁古董的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重新构想者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, national Republicans are determined to discredit the statewide recount underway in Florida as illegitimate and fraudulent.
sentences.zh: 今天，全国共和党人坚决将佛罗里达州正在进行的州级重新计票斥为非法和欺诈。

sentences.en: What Democrats have learned from the last time Republicans used that strategy.
sentences.zh: 民主党人从上次共和党人使用该策略的经历中吸取了什么教训。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, November 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月14日，星期三。

sentences.en: Uh, do we have Tallahassee?
sentences.zh: 呃，我们连线到塔拉哈西了吗？

sentences.en: Sorry, yeah.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，连上了。

sentences.en: Can you guys hear me now?
sentences.zh: 你们现在能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: Oh, it's Jeremy.
sentences.zh: 哦，是杰里米。

sentences.en: Hey, Jeremy.
sentences.zh: 嘿，杰里米。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Hey, handsome Jeremy.
sentences.zh: 嘿，帅哥杰里米。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: What a face for radio I have.
sentences.zh: 我这张脸还真适合做广播。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleagues, Maggie Haverman in Washington and Jeremy Peters in Tallahassee, Florida.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事，在华盛顿的玛吉·哈弗曼和在佛罗里达州塔拉哈西的杰里米·彼得斯。

sentences.en: Jeremy, this is probably going to be you with Florida.
sentences.zh: 杰里米，佛罗里达州这部分可能要由你来报道了。

sentences.en: When the polls close on Tuesday night in Florida, what do we see?
sentences.zh: 当周二晚间佛罗里达州的投票站关闭时，我们看到了什么？

sentences.en: So there are two big races going on in Florida, the governor's race and the race for United States Senate.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州当时有两场大选正在进行，州长竞选和美国参议院议员竞选。

sentences.en: And by the end of the evening, it looks like Republicans are in place to win both of those.
sentences.zh: 到傍晚结束时，看起来共和党人有望赢得这两场选举。

sentences.en: A big day and a big night for Republicans here in Florida.
sentences.zh: 对于佛罗里达州的共和党人来说，这是伟大的一天和伟大的夜晚。

sentences.en: Thank you, Florida, for your support.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，佛罗里达，感谢你们的支持。

sentences.en: Good morning, Maria.
sentences.zh: 早上好，玛丽亚。

sentences.en: It was a big night for Republicans here in Florida.
sentences.zh: 对于佛罗里达州的共和党人来说，这是一个伟大的夜晚。

sentences.en: But let's take a look first at that Senate race because we're calling...
sentences.zh: 但让我们首先来看看那场参议院选举，因为我们宣布……

sentences.en: In the Senate race, you have the state's current governor, Rick Scott, running to unseat the Democratic incumbent, Bill Nelson.
sentences.zh: 在参议院竞选中，该州现任州长里克·斯科特参选，试图击败民主党现任议员比尔·纳尔逊。

sentences.en: ...in the Senate for 18 years.
sentences.zh: ……在参议院任职18年。

sentences.en: So that was a big switch over...
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的转变……

sentences.en: And that's a pretty pivotal race because it's going to determine how comfortable the Republicans' majority is in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 这是一场非常关键的竞选，因为它将决定共和党人在参议院的多数优势会有多稳固。

sentences.en: And speaking of Florida, we're going to look at this governor's race.
sentences.zh: 说到佛罗里达州，我们将关注这场州长竞选。

sentences.en: An update here.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个最新消息。

sentences.en: Ron DeSantis...
sentences.zh: 罗恩·德桑蒂斯……

sentences.en: In the governor's race, you have Ron DeSantis.
sentences.zh: 在州长竞选中，有罗恩·德桑蒂斯。

sentences.en: I'd like to thank our president for standing by me when...
sentences.zh: 我要感谢我们的总统，在我……的时候支持我

sentences.en: This kind of Trump-styled Republican who became famous for running an ad that featured his young son building a wall.
sentences.zh: 这种特朗普风格的共和党人，因制作了一则以他年幼的儿子用玩具积木建墙为特色的竞选广告而一举成名。

sentences.en: ...out of toy bricks.
sentences.zh: ……用玩具积木搭的墙。

sentences.en: Mr. President, I look forward to working with you.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，我期待与您合作。

sentences.en: And it looks like he has defeated Andrew Gillum.
sentences.zh: 看起来他已经击败了安德鲁·吉伦。

sentences.en: We recognize that, you know, we didn't win it tonight.
sentences.zh: 我们承认，你知道，我们今晚没能赢得这场竞选。

sentences.en: ...who would become the state's first African-American governor.
sentences.zh: ……他将成为该州第一位非洲裔美国州长。

sentences.en: But that does not appear to be happening on election night.
sentences.zh: 但选举之夜似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: Earlier this evening, I called Mr. Ron DeSantis...
sentences.zh: 今天早些时候，我打电话给罗恩·德桑蒂斯先生……

sentences.en: ...and congratulated him on what we expect will be him as the next governor of the great state of Florida.
sentences.zh: ……并祝贺他，预计他将成为伟大的佛罗里达州的下一任州长。

sentences.en: So this starts to look like a Republican wipeout in a state that is considered a bellwether for the country, Florida.
sentences.zh: 因此，这开始看起来像是一场共和党在佛罗里达州的完胜，而该州一直被认为是全国的风向标。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And because it's Florida, it's really close, but decisive enough that the Republicans feel very confident as they go to sleep that night.
sentences.zh: 而且因为这是佛罗里达州，差距真的很小，但结果足够决定性，以至于共和党人在那天晚上入睡时感到非常自信。

sentences.en: Then, overnight, the vote totals continue to trickle in.
sentences.zh: 然后，在夜间，选票总数继续零星增加。

sentences.en: Of the state's 67 counties, Palm Beach and Broward counties were still counting votes Saturday.
sentences.zh: 在该州的67个县中，棕榈滩县和布劳沃德县在周六仍在点算选票。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: For Senate candidate Republican Governor Rick Scott, the vote totals are narrowing.
sentences.zh: 对于参议院候选人、共和党州长里克·斯科特来说，得票差距正在缩小。

sentences.en: Democratic Tallahassee Mayor Andrew Gillum has now narrowed the lead to 0.47 of a percentage point.
sentences.zh: 民主党塔拉哈西市长安德鲁·吉伦目前已将领先优势缩小到0.47个百分点。

sentences.en: And then just yesterday, the Republican leads shrunk even more.
sentences.zh: 就在昨天，共和党人的领先优势进一步缩小。

sentences.en: Both Republicans see their leads cut considerably.
sentences.zh: 两名共和党人的领先优势都被大幅削减。

sentences.en: The tallies between Republican Governor Rick Scott and incumbent Democrat Bill Nelson are so narrow, it could be within the margin requiring an additional manual recount.
sentences.zh: 共和党州长里克·斯科特与民主党现任议员比尔·纳尔逊之间的得票统计差距如此之小，以至于可能落入需要进行额外人工重新计票的微小差距之内。

sentences.en: They don't just feed the ballots into machines now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在不仅仅是把选票喂给机器。

sentences.en: Now they're going to take them out and hand-inspect them.
sentences.zh: 现在他们要把选票拿出来进行人工检查。

sentences.en: It looks like that's where it's heading here.
sentences.zh: 看起来事情正朝着这个方向发展。

sentences.en: Razor-fin margins in the battle for Florida's governor.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州长之争的差距极其微弱。

sentences.en: Democrat Andrew Gillum has now retracted his election night concession.
sentences.zh: 民主党人安德鲁·吉伦现已收回他在选举之夜的认输声明。

sentences.en: Replacing my words of concession with an uncompromised and unapologetic call that we count every single vote.
sentences.zh: 用坚定不移、毫无歉意的呼吁取代我承认失败的言辞，我们要求点算每一张选票。

sentences.en: We count every vote.
sentences.zh: 我们要点算每一张选票。

sentences.en: And I say this recognizing that my fate in this may or may not change.
sentences.zh: 我说这话时认识到，我在这场选举中的命运可能会也可能不会改变。

sentences.en: You know, let's be clear here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们要把话说清楚。

sentences.en: The Republican candidates in both races still have at this point a pretty significant advantage.
sentences.zh: 在这两场竞选中，共和党候选人目前仍然拥有相当明显的优势。

sentences.en: But it's close enough that the automatic recount called for in the law is triggered.
sentences.zh: 但差距已经小到足以触发法律规定的自动重新计票。

sentences.en: And the state appears headed toward a statewide recount in all 67 counties.
sentences.zh: 该州似乎正走向在全部67个县进行全州范围的重新计票。

sentences.en: So with these two races in Florida, governor and senator, hanging in the balance, how did Democrats start to respond to this situation?
sentences.zh: 因此，随着佛罗里达州的州长和参议员这两场竞选悬而未决，民主党人开始如何应对这一局面？

sentences.en: It's become obvious that Mr. Scott cannot oversee the process in a fair and impartial way.
sentences.zh: 很明显，斯科特先生无法以公平公正的方式监督这一过程。

sentences.en: And he should remove himself from the recount process.
sentences.zh: 他应该退出重新计票程序。

sentences.en: People must have confidence in the integrity of the election.
sentences.zh: 人们必须对选举的公正性充满信心。

sentences.en: So Democrats have looked at this recount, which was legally mandated in Florida as a way to underscore something that they say is going on with Republicans, not just in Florida,
sentences.zh: 因此，民主党人将这场在佛罗里达州法律规定的重新计票视为一种方式，用来强调他们所说的共和党人正在做的事情，不仅在佛罗里达州，

sentences.en: but nationally, which is trying to undermine faith in democracy itself, trying to undermine faith that elections are sound and being held appropriately.
sentences.zh: 而且在全国范围内，他们正试图破坏对民主本身的信仰，试图破坏对选举健全且妥善举行的信心。

sentences.en: And what do we see Republicans doing that would support that characterization by Democrats?
sentences.zh: 我们看到共和党人做了什么来印证民主党人的这种定性？

sentences.en: The main issue is, among other things, trying to protest a legally mandated recount.
sentences.zh: 主要问题之一是，除其他外，试图抗议法律规定的重新计票。

sentences.en: We've seen that before, but they are doing it with claims of fraud.
sentences.zh: 我们以前见过这种情况，但他们这次是以存在欺诈的指控来这样做的。

sentences.en: I think they just cut open an alligator in the Everglades and found two more boxes of ballots down in Broward County.
sentences.zh: 我想他们刚刚剖开大沼泽地里的一条短吻鳄，又在布劳沃德县发现了两箱选票。

sentences.en: Every Floridian should be concerned there may be rampant fraud happening in Palm Beach and Broward County.
sentences.zh: 每个佛罗里达人都应该担心棕榈滩县和布劳沃德县可能正在发生猖獗的选举欺诈。

sentences.en: Election fraud charges are flying.
sentences.zh: 关于选举欺诈的指控满天飞。

sentences.en: Florida, quote, it's clear the Democrats' goal here is not to count every vote fairly, but to steal an election.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州，引述：“很明显，民主党人的目标不是公平地点算每一张选票，而是窃取一场选举。”

sentences.en: I will not sit idly by while unethical liberals try to steal this election from the great people of Florida.
sentences.zh: 当不道德的自由派试图从伟大的佛罗里达人民手中窃取这场选举时，我绝不会袖手旁观。

sentences.en: And it's mostly in their language, but they are infecting the process with a tinge of something improper taking place.
sentences.zh: 这主要体现在他们的措辞中，但他们在整个过程中灌输了一种不正当行为正在发生的暗示。

sentences.en: National Republicans and Republicans locally in Florida have said Democrats are trying to find a way to reverse the result here.
sentences.zh: 全国共和党人和佛罗里达州地方共和党人表示，民主党人正试图寻找方法来逆转那里的结果。

sentences.en: They have pointed to the fact that Republicans are up and that there aren't enough ballots, and so Democrats are looking for a way to try to undo that.
sentences.zh: 他们指出共和党人领先且选票不足的事实，因此民主党人正在寻找方法试图抹杀这一结果。

sentences.en: Democrats obviously deny that.
sentences.zh: 民主党人显然否认这一点。

sentences.en: But if history shows that only the tiniest fraction of elections are ever reversed based on recounts, then isn't a recount really just a validation of the winning candidate?
sentences.zh: 但如果历史表明只有极小一部分选举结果会因重新计票而被推翻，那么重新计票不就只是一种对获胜候选人的再次确认吗？

sentences.en: It just gives you a clearer picture of exactly how much they won by.
sentences.zh: 它只是让你更清楚地了解他们究竟赢了多少票。

sentences.en: And if that's the case, why are Republicans resisting this or trying to undermine it?
sentences.zh: 既然如此，为什么共和党人要抵制或试图破坏它？

sentences.en: Because a big part of the conservative political identity, especially over the last decade, is to question the legitimacy of American elections,
sentences.zh: 因为保守派政治身份的一个重要部分，尤其是在过去十年里，就是质疑美国选举的合法性，

sentences.en: to push the unproven and often unfounded claim that Democrats cheat and steal and stuff the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 推卸未经证实且通常毫无根据的指控，即民主党人作弊、偷窃和塞选票。

sentences.en: And that's why Republicans have lost in certain close races.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么共和党人在某些势均力敌的竞选中会落败的原因。

sentences.en: What recounts are supposed to do is reaffirm the public's faith that the election they've just seen happen, a very close, close election,
sentences.zh: 重新计票本该做的是重新确立公众对他们刚刚经历的这场非常非常接近的选举的信心，

sentences.en: is indeed legitimate and that they can trust the outcome.
sentences.zh: 确信它确实是合法的，并且他们可以信任选举结果。

sentences.en: But there's this pattern now that Republicans have picked up on where they can kind of combine these arguments that they've long made about voter fraud and the infection of the electoral process by people who are out to cheat.
sentences.zh: 但现在共和党人养成了一种模式，他们可以把长期以来关于选民欺诈的论点，以及企图作弊的人对选举过程的污染，这些论点结合起来。

sentences.en: And this is like the perfect storm of that happening in Florida.
sentences.zh: 这就像是这一切在佛罗里达州发生的完美风暴。

sentences.en: And they seize on it.
sentences.zh: 他们抓住了这个机会。

sentences.en: There is tremendous political power for the Republicans in claiming that the Democrats are trying to steal what is to them a settled election.
sentences.zh: 对于共和党人来说，声称民主党人正试图窃取对他们来说已经尘埃落定的选举，具有巨大的政治力量。

sentences.en: And that motivates the Republican conservative base in a big way.
sentences.zh: 这极大地激励了共和党保守派基层。

sentences.en: In the broadest terms,
sentences.zh: 从最广泛的意义上讲，

sentences.en: what you're seeing right now in Florida by Republicans in terms of strategy bridges all the way back to the 2000 presidential election where you had Republicans decrying Democrats
sentences.zh: 你现在在佛罗里达州看到共和党人在战略上所做的一切，一直可以追溯到2000年的总统大选，当时共和党人谴责民主党人，

sentences.en: and suggesting that they were using dishonest means to try to grab the state back in favor of Al Gore.
sentences.zh: 并暗示他们正在使用不诚实的手段试图将该州夺回以支持阿尔·戈尔。

sentences.en: It feels very similar and evocative.
sentences.zh: 感觉非常相似且唤起人们的回忆。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: I'm Tom Brokaw in New York.
sentences.zh: 我是纽约的汤姆·布罗考。

sentences.en: It's been a long campaign.
sentences.zh: 这是一场漫长的竞选。

sentences.en: It appears it will be a long and exciting evening before we know who is the next president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 在我们知道谁将是下一任美国总统之前，看来这将是一个漫长而激动人心的夜晚。

sentences.en: You have a strikingly similar situation on election night and the immediate aftermath as you do today.
sentences.zh: 在选举之夜及其后的紧凑时刻，你面临着与今天惊人相似的局面。

sentences.en: CNN announces that we call Florida in the Al Gore column.
sentences.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网宣布我们将佛罗里达州划入阿尔·戈尔的阵营。

sentences.en: This is a state both campaigns desperately wanted.
sentences.zh: 这是两个竞选团队都极力争取的州。

sentences.en: Stand by.
sentences.zh: 请稍候。

sentences.en: Stand by.
sentences.zh: 请稍候。

sentences.en: CNN right now is moving our earlier declaration of Florida.
sentences.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网现在正在撤回我们早些时候对佛罗里达州的宣布。

sentences.en: George Bush, governor of Texas, will become the 43rd president of the United States at 18 minutes past 2 o'clock Eastern time.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州州长乔治·布什将于东部时间2点18分成为美国第43任总统。

sentences.en: CNN declares...
sentences.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网宣布……

sentences.en: Gore calls George W.
sentences.zh: 戈尔在选举之夜打电话给小乔治·

sentences.en: Bush on election night thinking he's lost and he concedes to Bush.
sentences.zh: 布什，以为自己输了，并向布什认输。

sentences.en: And they look at the numbers a little bit more closely in the Gore campaign and they grab Gore just as he is about to go on stage and deliver his concession speech in Nashville and convince him,
sentences.zh: 戈尔竞选团队更仔细地查看了数字，就在戈尔即将走上纳什维尔的舞台发表认输演讲时，他们拉住戈尔并说服他，

sentences.en: no, this is not over, because Al Gore has recanted that concession that he gave earlier on this evening.
sentences.zh: 不，还没有结束，因为阿尔·戈尔已经收回了他今天早些时候做出的认输声明。

sentences.en: So stand by.
sentences.zh: 所以请稍候。

sentences.en: I'll try to get a little bit more information.
sentences.zh: 我试着获取更多信息。

sentences.en: He calls George Bush back and retracts his concession.
sentences.zh: 他回电话给乔治·布什并撤回了他的认输。

sentences.en: This race is simply too close to call.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选实在是难分胜负。

sentences.en: And until the results, the recount is concluded and the results of Florida become official, our campaign continues.
sentences.zh: 在结果出来、重新计票结束且佛罗里达州的结果成为官方正式结果之前，我们的竞选仍在继续。

sentences.en: Let us be the votes.
sentences.zh: 让我们成为选票。

sentences.en: Let us be the votes.
sentences.zh: 让我们成为选票。

sentences.zh: 让我们成为选票。

sentences.en: Let us be the votes.
sentences.zh: 让我们成为选票。

sentences.en: And what you have after that is this protracted recount fight...
sentences.zh: 在那之后，你面临的就是这场旷日持久的重新计票之战……

sentences.en: Protests will continue until they...
sentences.zh: 抗议活动将继续，直到他们……

sentences.en: ...in the courts, on the streets in protests, and in the news media in a battle for the hearts and minds of Americans.
sentences.zh: ……在法庭上、在街头的抗议中，以及在新闻媒体中展开了一场争夺美国人心的战役。

sentences.en: Tell us a little bit more about that.
sentences.zh: 给我们多讲讲那个。

sentences.en: What did Republicans do back then, in 2000, that would be looked back at now as a kind of inspiration?
sentences.zh: 当年（2000年）共和党人做了什么，会被现在的人们视为一种灵感来源？

sentences.en: So the Republican Party and the Bush campaign never stopped treating the recount like it was anything other than a campaign.
sentences.zh: 所以共和党人和布什竞选团队从未停止将重新计票当作一场竞选来对待。

sentences.en: Two weeks after the presidential election, a court has decided that Florida's deadline for counting votes and certifying votes was not a deadline at all.
sentences.zh: 总统大选两周后，法院裁定佛罗里达州统计选票和认证选票的截止日期根本不是什么截止日期。

sentences.en: That was very different from how Al Gore and his team approached it.
sentences.zh: 这与阿尔·戈尔及其团队的处理方式截然不同。

sentences.en: I firmly believe that the will of the people should prevail.
sentences.zh: 我坚信人民的意志应该占上风。

sentences.en: And I am gratified that the court's decision will allow us to honor that simple constitutional principle.
sentences.zh: 我感到欣慰的是，法院的裁决将使我们能够兑现这一简单的宪法原则。

sentences.en: There's this very telling scene recounted in Jeffrey Toobin's book on the Florida recount of 2000 where the Gore campaign staff,
sentences.zh: 杰弗里·图宾关于2000年佛罗里达州重新计票的书中有这样一个非常说明问题的场景，当时戈尔竞选团队的工作人员，

sentences.en: in flying down its young volunteers to help with the recount, tells them all to take off their campaign pin so that they are not a part of the Gore campaign anymore.
sentences.zh: 在空运年轻志愿者去协助重新计票时，告诉他们所有人摘下竞选徽章，这样他们就不再是戈尔竞选团队的一部分了。

sentences.en: They are there for something very different.
sentences.zh: 他们到那里是为了某种非常不同的事情。

sentences.en: George W.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，小乔治·

sentences.en: Bush and the Republican Party, on the other hand, saw this as a fight they needed not only to win in court, but they needed to win in the court of public opinion.
sentences.zh: 布什和共和党人认为，这是一场他们不仅需要在法庭上取胜，还需要在公众舆论法庭上取胜的战斗。

sentences.en: The Bush campaign representative, James Baker, was displeased.
sentences.zh: 布什竞选团队代表詹姆斯·贝克对此感到不满。

sentences.en: It is not fair to change the rules and standards governing the counting or recounting of votes after it appears that one side has concluded that is the only way to get the votes it needs.
sentences.zh: 在一方认定这是获得所需选票的唯一途径之后，去更改管理选票统计或重新统计的规则和标准是不公平的。

sentences.en: Republican demonstrators cheered as the already counted ballots were returned to elections headquarters, and a well-known former presidential candidate, Bob Dole,
sentences.zh: 共和党示威者欢呼雀跃，此前已被点算的选票被退回选举总部，一位著名的前总统候选人鲍勃·多尔

sentences.en: said it was not fair to count those dimpled chads.
sentences.zh: 表示，去点算那些带有凹痕的选票是不公平的。

sentences.en: That meant mobilizing demonstrators.
sentences.zh: 这意味着动员示威者。

sentences.en: Adding more fuel to the fire, GOP protester C.
sentences.zh: 火上浇油的是，共和党抗议者C.

sentences.en: Geller with a ballot in hand, leading them to charge he had stolen a ballot.
sentences.zh: 格勒拿着一张选票，引得人们指责他偷了一张选票。

sentences.en: This is the most brazen attempt by the Gore people and the Democrat machine and the thugs in that building to hijack the American presidency.
sentences.zh: 这是戈尔阵营、民主党机器以及那栋大楼里的暴徒对美国总统职权最肆无忌惮的篡夺企图。

sentences.en: And part of the street fight aspect of the Bush campaign's strategy is to deploy demonstrators who are actually Republican staffers, some of them from Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 布什阵营街头战策略的一部分，就是部署实际上是共和党工作人员的示威者，其中有些人来自国会山。

sentences.en: And they sparked this incident that became known somewhat derisively as the Brooks Brothers riot,
sentences.zh: 他们引发了这起被略带嘲讽地称为“布鲁克斯兄弟骚乱”的事件，

sentences.en: where a number of these staffers gathered in the Miami-Dade building where the recount by hand was taking place, saying that there was cheating going on inside,
sentences.zh: 当时，许多此类工作人员聚集在迈阿密-戴德大楼里，当时正在那里进行手工重新计票，他们声称里面正在发生作弊，

sentences.en: that this process was illegitimate and that the Democrats were trying to steal the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 这一进程是非法的，民主党人正试图窃取总统大选。

sentences.en: That protest that day shut down the recount in Miami-Dade, and it never resumed after that, and that could have been the difference that allowed George W.
sentences.zh: 那天的那场抗议活动迫使迈阿密-戴德的重新计票中断，此后就再也没有恢复，而这可能正是让小乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush to keep his advantage in Florida.
sentences.zh: 布什得以保持在佛罗里达州优势的关键所在。

sentences.en: We believe that Miami-Dade County Canvassing Board made the right decision for the right reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们相信迈阿密-戴德县选举计票委员会做出了正确的决定，理由也是充分的。

sentences.en: They, in essence, said that there is a limit, that there are rational reasons for us to reject this idea of a rush to judgment in an attempt to try and reconstruct an election.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他们是在说这是有限度的，我们拒绝这种试图仓促得出结论以拼凑出一场选举的想法，是有理有据的。

sentences.en: As I recall it, eventually, recounts are done after the election that show George W.
sentences.zh: 据我回忆，最终，选举后的重新计票表明，如果重新计票进行下去的话，小乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush would have won if the recount had proceeded.
sentences.zh: 布什本来就会获胜。

sentences.en: Other scenarios, counting a broader set of ballots, suggest Gore might have prevailed.
sentences.zh: 其他涵盖更广泛选票的方案则表明，戈尔可能会获胜。

sentences.en: But I guess that's all sort of beside the point, because the strategy was to stop the recount and to sow doubt.
sentences.zh: 但我想这已经无关紧要了，因为这一策略的目的就是停止重新计票并播下怀疑的种子。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And if you look back then at the way that Republicans were casting doubt on the integrity of the electoral process and accusing Democrats of effectively stealing an election or trying to,
sentences.zh: 如果你回看当时共和党人对选举过程公正性提出质疑的方式，以及指控民主党人实际上窃取或试图窃取选举的行为，

sentences.en: that is what you hear an awful lot today from Republicans and from President Trump himself when they are implying that Democrats cheat their way to victory.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，如今共和党人和特朗普总统本人在暗示民主党人通过作弊赢得胜利时，充斥着大量这样的话语。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that you are seeing Democrats more mobilized this time to suggest that the Republicans are acting just in total bad faith.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这一次你可以看到民主党人更加积极地行动起来，指出共和党人的行为完全是出于恶意。

sentences.en: But there is something similar going on where Democrats are basically saying we need to have every vote counted and Republicans are essentially saying you are all focusing on the wrong story.
sentences.zh: 但其中也有相似之处，民主党人基本上是在说我们需要统计每一张选票，而共和党人则本质上是在说你们所有人都关注错了方向。

sentences.en: The right story is the Democrats are trying to steal this.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题在于民主党人正试图窃取这场选举。

sentences.en: And there's absolutely no evidence of fraud taking place.
sentences.zh: 然而绝对没有任何证据表明存在欺诈行为。

sentences.en: This is what judges have said.
sentences.zh: 法官们就是这么说的。

sentences.en: This has been shown over and over.
sentences.zh: 这一点已经一次又一次地得到证明。

sentences.en: So, again, as you did in 2000, to Jeremy's point, you have Republicans treating this like an extension of the run-up to Election Day.
sentences.zh: 因此，重申杰里米的话，正如他们在2000年所做的那样，共和党人再次将此视为大选日临近前夕的延伸。

sentences.en: I do think it's important to point out that there are political motivations on both sides as they fight through this recount.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为有一点很重要，需要指出的是，双方在争夺这场重新计票的过程中都有各自的政治动机。

sentences.en: Democrats say they want to count every vote.
sentences.zh: 民主党人表示他们希望统计每一张选票。

sentences.en: But Democrats are also trying to remove standards and safeguards that would allow vote counters to determine whether or not a ballot is fraudulent.
sentences.zh: 但民主党人同时也试图移除那些能让验票员判断选票是否存在欺诈的标准和保障措施。

sentences.en: They're basically saying that the standards that exist in evaluating the signatures on ballots are too rigid and they shouldn't be applied.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在说，目前评估选票签名的标准过于僵化，不应该被应用。

sentences.en: And that leaves you in a situation where you don't really have a standard to judge whether or not a ballot is valid.
sentences.zh: 这就导致了一种情况：你实际上没有一个标准来判断一张选票是否有效。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is troublesome to people on both sides of this.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这让这场争端双方的人都感到棘手。

sentences.en: So, the Democrats are trying to loosen the rules after the election in a way that could clearly help Democrats in a recount.
sentences.zh: 因此，民主党人正试图在选后放宽规则，这种做法显然能在重新计票中对民主党有利。

sentences.en: Yes, they're arguing that point in court.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们正在法庭上力争这一点。

sentences.en: So, Democrats are more actively involved this time than they were in 2000 in trying to play this game that Republicans have been doing so effectively.
sentences.zh: 因此，与2000年相比，民主党人这次更加积极地参与进来，试图玩转共和党人一直以来玩得如此之溜的游戏。

sentences.en: What else is different this time than from 2000?
sentences.zh: 这次与2000年还有什么不同？

sentences.en: It's a great question and it's answered with one word, which is Trump.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，用一个词就能回答，那就是：特朗普。

sentences.en: Almost immediately from Europe Saturday, President Trump lashed out at Democrats, tweeting, trying to steal two big elections in Florida.
sentences.zh: 周六，特朗普总统几乎立刻就从欧洲对民主党人进行了猛烈抨击，他在推特上称其正试图窃取佛罗里达州的两次大选。

sentences.en: We are watching closely.
sentences.zh: 我们正在密切关注。

sentences.en: The president has been involved in this recount and in trying to put his thumb on the scale in ways that we've really never seen a U.S.
sentences.zh: 总统一直卷入这场重新计票中，并试图以我们从未见过的美国总统所用的方式，

sentences.en: president do.
sentences.zh: 对天平施加影响。

sentences.en: President Trump today tweeted,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统今天发推称，

sentences.en: the Florida election should be called in favor of Rick Scott and Ron DeSantis and that large numbers of new ballots showed up out of nowhere and many ballots are missing or forged.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州选举应该宣布里克·斯科特和罗恩·德桑蒂斯获胜，因为大量新选票不知从哪里冒出来，且许多选票失踪或伪造。

sentences.en: An honest vote count is no longer possible.
sentences.zh: 诚实的计票已不再可能。

sentences.en: Ballots massively infected must go with election night.
sentences.zh: 被严重污染的选票必须服从选举之夜的结果。

sentences.en: He has offered an opinion on this.
sentences.zh: 他对此发表了看法。

sentences.en: He has described the ballots and the process as, quote unquote, infected.
sentences.zh: 他将选票和选举过程描述为所谓的“受污染的”。

sentences.en: Tweeting in part, you mean they are just now finding votes in Florida and Georgia, but the election was on Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 他在推文中部分写道，你的意思是他们现在才在佛罗里达州和佐治亚州发现选票，可选举明明是在周二进行的吗？

sentences.en: Let's blame the Russians and demand an immediate apology from President Putin.
sentences.zh: 把这怪罪到俄罗斯人头上，并要求普京总统立即道歉。

sentences.en: Now, Republicans will privately say they wish he were being more restrained, but they certainly are not saying that publicly.
sentences.zh: 现在，共和党人在私下里会表示希望他能更克制一些，但他们在公开场合绝对不会这么说。

sentences.en: Why would Republicans want him to be more restrained?
sentences.zh: 为什么共和党人希望他更克制一点？

sentences.en: Because it could create a backlash because when he says things, it tends to create an equal and opposite, if not greater, reaction among voters who oppose him.
sentences.zh: 因为这可能会引发反弹，当他说某些话时，往往会在反对他的选民中激起同等甚至更强烈的对立反应。

sentences.en: And because there's always the risk that his involvement could end up tainting a court proceeding and that a judge could see it that way.
sentences.zh: 而且，始终存在这样一种风险，即他的介入最终可能会玷污法庭诉讼程序，导致法官也这样看待此事。

sentences.en: So they would rather he not get involved.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们宁愿他不要卷入其中。

sentences.en: And why exactly is President Trump so invested in this situation in Florida?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么特朗普总统对佛罗里达州的局势如此投入呢？

sentences.en: I think for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 我认为原因有几个。

sentences.en: One, he understands it's an important state electorically.
sentences.zh: 第一，他明白这是一个具有重要选举意义的州。

sentences.en: Number two, it's a state where in the DeSantis campaign, he and his aides essentially took over DeSantis' race.
sentences.zh: 第二，在德桑蒂斯的竞选活动中，他与助手基本上接管了德桑蒂斯的竞选。

sentences.en: They installed their own people.
sentences.zh: 他们安插了自己的人手。

sentences.en: They sent their own advisers in to run it.
sentences.zh: 他们派出了自己的顾问去运营。

sentences.en: He saw DeSantis as something of a mini-me.
sentences.zh: 他把德桑蒂斯看作某种“小号的自己”。

sentences.en: And in the case of Rick Scott, Scott had been uncertain how closely he wanted to hug Trump, which Trump took personally.
sentences.zh: 而在里克·斯科特的事上，斯科特曾一度不确定自己该跟特朗普走得多近，特朗普对此感到被冒犯了。

sentences.en: And it turned out that Rick Scott did need him.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，里克·斯科特确实需要他。

sentences.en: So I think for all of those reasons, he sees two elections that he thinks have a lot to do with him.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为基于所有这些原因，他看到了两场他认为与他息息相关的选举。

sentences.en: If both sides, first Republicans and now in response Democrats, are treating recounts as extensions of campaigns based on what they learned in 2000,
sentences.zh: 如果双方——先是共和党人，现在是作为回应的民主党人——都根据2000年吸取的教训，将重新计票视为竞选活动的延伸，

sentences.en: and we're now seeing that unfolding in Florida, where does this all go?
sentences.zh: 而我们现在又看到这一幕在佛罗里达州上演，这一切最终将走向何方？

sentences.en: Not just in Florida, but the next time there's another big recount.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是在佛罗里达州，还有下一次发生重大重新计票的时候。

sentences.en: I think that you can assume that it gets more political.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以预料到事情会变得更加政治化。

sentences.en: I think that you can assume that the tactics become nastier.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以预料到战术会变得更加恶劣。

sentences.en: I think you can assume the language becomes louder and more accusatory.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以预料到措辞会变得更加激烈、更具指责性。

sentences.en: I think that you are seeing the systemic degradation of norms and a faith in institutions, and everything is getting replaced with being about politics only.
sentences.zh: 我认为你正在看到规范的系统性退化以及对机构信任的丧失，一切都被纯粹的政治所取代。

sentences.en: So yet another institution that Americans have lost to politics.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是美国人因政治而失去的又一个机构。

sentences.en: The one reasonable certainty that Americans had about elections, in addition to that they would be the first Tuesday after the first Monday of November,
sentences.zh: 美国人对选举仅存的合乎情理的确定性，除了选举定在11月第一个星期一之后的第一个星期二之外，

sentences.en: is that they would be conducted with civic-mindedness.
sentences.zh: 就是选举将秉持公民意识来进行。

sentences.en: That there would be rules and integrity that are adhered to, and that it wouldn't be all about what party you're involved in.
sentences.zh: 那就是会有规则和诚信受到遵守，而不是完全取决于你加入了哪个政党。

sentences.en: But those norms, like a lot else in our political system right now, have degraded.
sentences.zh: 但这些规范，就像我们当前政治系统中的许多其他东西一样，已经退化了。

sentences.en: Jeremy, Maggie, thank you both very much.
sentences.zh: 杰里米、玛吉，非常感谢二位。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Election workers across the state are racing against the clock right now to get every vote counted before Thursday's deadline.
sentences.zh: 全州的选举工作人员目前正与时间赛跑，以便在周四的截止日期前统计每一张选票。

sentences.en: Thursday, 3 p.m.
sentences.zh: 周四下午3点。

sentences.en: All 67 counties must have their recount numbers in, or, according to law, those votes won't be counted.
sentences.zh: 所有67个县必须提交其重新计票数据，否则根据法律，这些选票将不被计算在内。

sentences.en: Broward is confident they will make that.
sentences.zh: 布劳沃德县有信心能赶上。

sentences.en: However, up in Palm Beach County, where they have older machines, they do seriously worry that they can make that Thursday deadline.
sentences.zh: 然而，在拥有较老机器的棕榈滩县，他们确实严重担心自己无法赶上周四的截止日期。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶时代的夜总会当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍爱的传家宝去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个，

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 装满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.zh: 现在即可在您喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日新闻简报《交易手册》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市“交易手册”峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些最具影响力的人物，包括J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at The DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以亲眼见证其中一些毫无保留、未经滤镜的对话实时发生。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获取我们所有新闻报道一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收听。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, fearing a crackdown by federal regulators, the company that dominates the e-cigarette market in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周二，由于担心遭到联邦监管机构的打击，统治美国电子烟市场的公司

sentences.en: said it will stop selling most of its flavored products at retail stores and will no longer promote them on social media.
sentences.zh: 表示将停止在零售店销售大部分调味产品，并不再在社交媒体上对其进行宣传。

sentences.en: The proportion of high school teenagers using e-cigarettes has reached nothing short of an epidemic level, in my view,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，高中青少年使用电子烟的比例已经达到了堪称流行病的水平，

sentences.en: and it requires us to step in and take dramatic action to try to curtail this.
sentences.zh: 这需要我们介入并采取戏剧性的行动来试图遏制这一现象。

sentences.en: The company, Juul, is the subject of intense scrutiny by the FDA, whose commissioner, Scott Gottlieb,
sentences.zh: 这家名为Juul的公司正受到美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）的密切审查，该局局长斯科特·戈特利布

sentences.en: had planned to ban the flavored products at many stores after discovering that underage use of vaping products has surged.
sentences.zh: 在发现未成年人使用电子烟产品的激增现象后，曾计划在许多商店禁售这些调味产品。

sentences.en: A lot of this youth use is being driven by one manufacturer, and particularly Juul.
sentences.zh: 这种年轻人使用的现象很大程度上是由一家制造商推动的，尤其是Juul。

sentences.en: I think we need to acknowledge that.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要承认这一点。

sentences.en: Juul has denied that it markets to children under 18, but its flavored products, like mango and cream,
sentences.zh: Juul否认其向18岁以下的儿童进行营销，但其芒果味和奶油味等调味产品

sentences.en: have prompted accusations that the company is directly targeting underage customers.
sentences.zh: 引发了指责，称该公司直接将目标对准了未成年消费者。

sentences.en: And in an unusual move, CNN sued the Trump administration on Tuesday in an effort to reinstate the press credentials of its chief White House correspondent, Jim Acosta.
sentences.zh: 在一次不同寻常的举动中，美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）于周二起诉了特朗普政府，试图恢复其白宫首席记者吉姆·阿科斯塔的记者证。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，总统先生。

sentences.en: I wanted to challenge you on one of the statements that you made in the tail end of the campaign in the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 我想就你在中期选举尾声时发表的其中一个声明向你提出质问。

sentences.en: Here we go.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Well, if you don't mind, Mr. President, that this caravan was an invasion.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你不介意的话，总统先生，这个大篷车队是一场入侵。

sentences.en: The White House had stripped his credential after a news conference last week,
sentences.zh: 在白宫上周举行新闻发布会剥夺他的记者证之后，

sentences.en: during which Acosta asked an unwelcome question about immigration and did not relinquish a microphone to a White House intern after the president tried to move on to another reporter.
sentences.zh: 阿科斯塔在会上提出了一个关于移民的不受欢迎的问题，并且在总统试图转向另一位记者时没有把麦克风交还给白宫实习生。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: That's not an invasion.
sentences.zh: 那不是入侵。

sentences.en: Honestly, I think you should let me run the country, you run CNN, and if you did it well, your ratings would be much better.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为你应该让我来管理国家，你来运营CNN，如果你能把它做好，你的收视率会好得多。

sentences.en: If I may ask one other question, Mr. President, if I may ask one other question, are you worried?
sentences.zh: 如果我可以问另一个问题，总统先生，如果我可以问另一个问题，你担心吗？

sentences.en: That's enough.
sentences.zh: 够了。

sentences.en: That's enough.
sentences.zh: 够了。

sentences.en: Mr. President, I was going to ask one of the other folks.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，我正准备问其他几位呢。

sentences.en: That's enough.
sentences.zh: 够了。

sentences.en: Pardon me, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 打扰一下，女士。

sentences.en: In its lawsuit, CNN argued that the removal of Acosta's White House press pass was a violation of his First Amendment right to freely report on the government.
sentences.zh: CNN在诉讼中辩称，撤销阿科斯塔的白宫记者证侵犯了他根据宪法第一修正案享有的自由报道政府的权利。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日简报》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶时代的夜总会当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍爱的传家宝去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个，

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 装满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在您喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。
